about: Château de Sales is the largest estate in Pomerol and home to the appellation’s only true château, a Louis XIII-style house built in the first half of the seventeenth century and listed as a historic monument since 1996. The same bloodline has held the land since 1464, when Bertrand de Sauvanelle took it over from Dominican monks; it has passed through the Sauvanelle, Desaigues, de Laage and de Lambert families since. Henri de Lambert enlarged and modernised the vineyard, his son Bruno ran it from 1982 to 2017, and a new generation of cousins took over in 2017.

The estate covers about 90 hectares in the north-western corner of Pomerol, with 47.6 hectares of vines in a single block, on small gravels and warm sands rich in iron oxide, the “crasse de fer” of the region. Merlot leads, with Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc. Grapes are hand-picked plot by plot and fermented in temperature-controlled concrete vats; the grand vin then ages about 12 to 18 months in French oak, only a minority of it new. Since 2017 the team has worked with Jean-Claude Berrouet, long the winemaker at Pétrus.

The 2020 is a fruit-driven, generous Pomerol: Decanter found juicy, bright red fruit, delicate and alive, James Suckling called it creamy and round, and Falstaff noted cherry, citrus peel and liquorice with silky, fine tannins. The Wine Advocate called it an attractive, elegantly fruit-driven Pomerol, and Wine Enthusiast credited the dominant Merlot for its richness and smooth texture. It is approachable now and has the balance to develop over the next decade or more.
